# Agent Sidecar Governance

## Runtime boundary

- Keep `[project].dependencies` empty; Agent Sidecar has zero runtime dependencies.
- Support Python 3.9 and newer in production code and public tooling.
- Keep the installed product within the Python standard-library boundary; add non-stdlib tools only to development extras.
- Treat `plugin/` (the dsh host-bridge TypeScript npm package) as the only sanctioned runtime-boundary exception; keep its Node toolchain — pnpm, vitest, and the tracked prebuilt `lib/` output — confined to `plugin/`.
- Let `plugin/` consume Agent Sidecar only through public contracts — the daemon Unix-socket protocol, CLI JSON, and read-only audit surfaces — never through Python internals.
- Keep the Python-side rules above unaffected by `plugin/`: `[project].dependencies` stays empty and the installed Python product stays standard-library only.

## Verification and contracts

- Run `python3 scripts/check.py` before handing off any change.
- Treat CLI commands, JSON, exit codes, configuration, and local protocols as public contracts.
- Update affected documentation and tests in the same change whenever a public contract changes.
- Add regression coverage for every new path and every bug fix.

## Sources of truth

- Follow `CONTRIBUTING.md` for development, review, branch, and release processes.
- Keep `README.md` and `README.zh.md` authoritative and synchronized for user-facing behavior.
- Keep `skills/agent-sidecar/SKILL.md` and `skills/agent-sidecar/reference.md` authoritative for agent integration and protocol details.
- Record user-observable changes in `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Branch and release integrity

- Keep `main` as the green development trunk and `release` as a fast-forward-only stable pointer to a CI-green `main` commit.
- Never create unique commits on `release`.
- Treat every published `v*` tag as immutable; never move, delete, or recreate one.

## Privacy and remote boundaries

- Never commit, log, or expose authentication tokens, raw transcripts, private Cursor data, credentials, or private machine paths.
- Keep token and Unix-socket files owner-private, and keep optional HTTP endpoints loopback-only.
- Export only synthetic, fully sanitized transcript fixtures.
- Keep SSH noninteractive and bounded; do not print remote secrets or session content, and clean temporary remote artifacts.

## Generated governance

- Edit governance only in canonical `.rules/*.mdc` sources or `.rules/compile-config.yaml`.
- Never hand-edit generated `AGENTS.md`, `.rules/.compile-hashes.json`, or other compiled rule surfaces.
- Regenerate and commit canonical sources and generated outputs together by following `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
